questions.question: Marked price of an article is Rs. 10500 and its selling price is Rs. 8820. What is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of an article = Rs. 10500

Selling price of an article = Rs. 8820

**Calculation:**

Discount = Marked price - Selling Price

⇒ Discount = 10500 - 8820 = Rs. 1680

So, Discount % = 1680/10500 × 100 = 1680/105 = 16%

**Hence, the correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: To complete a wall, Vijay takes 40 percent more time than Ramesh. If together they complete the wall in 25 days, then how much time will Vijay alone take to complete it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time Ratio (Vijay : Ramesh) = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5

Efficiency Ratio (Vijay : Ramesh) = 5 : 7 (Inversely proportional to time)

Combined Efficiency = 5 + 7 = 12 units/day

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Together Time = 12 × 25 = 300 units

Vijay's alone time = Total Work ÷ Vijay's Efficiency = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 days

**∴ The correct answer is 60 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Vijay and Ramesh together = 25 days

Vijay's time = Ramesh's time + 40% of Ramesh's time

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time is a:b, then the ratio of efficiency is b:a.

Total Work Formula

Work and Wages

questions.question: If 5P = 4Q, then what is the value of (P + Q) / P?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

5P = 4Q

**Formula Used:**

To find the value of (P + Q) / P

**Calculation:**

From the given equation,

5P = 4Q

Divide both sides by P:

5 = 4Q / P

Rearrange to solve for Q / P:

Q / P = 5 / 4

Now, (P + Q) / P can be written as:

(P / P + Q / P)

Substitute the value of Q / P:

(P / P + 5 / 4)

1 + 5 / 4

⇒ 1 + 1.25

⇒ 2.25 = 9/4

**The value of (P + Q) / P is 9/4.**

questions.question: Ramita alone can do a work in 100 days, Suman alone can do the same work in 120 days and Neetu alone can do the same work in 150 days. If they do that work together and they are paid Rs. 6000, then what is the share of Suman?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramita alone can do the work in 100 days.

Suman alone can do the work in 120 days.

Neetu alone can do the work in 150 days.

Total payment for the work = Rs. 6000

**Formula Used:**

Share of each person = (Individual's work rate / Sum of all work rates) × Total payment

**Calculation:**

Work rate of Ramita = 1/100

Work rate of Suman = 1/120

Work rate of Neetu = 1/150

Sum of all work rates = (1/100) + (1/120) + (1/150)

Sum of all work rates = (6 + 5 + 4)/600

Sum of all work rates = 15/600

Sum of all work rates = 1/40

Share of Suman = (Work rate of Suman / Sum of all work rates) × Total payment

Share of Suman = (1/120) ÷ (1/40) × 6000

Share of Suman = (1/120) × (40/1) × 6000

Share of Suman = 40/120 × 6000

Share of Suman = 1/3 × 6000

Share of Suman = 2000

**The share of Suman is Rs. 2000.**

questions.question: A merchant marks the price of his article 10 percent above the cost price. If he allows 5 percent discount, then what is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price is 10% above cost price.

Discount allowed is 5%.

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss Percentage = (Selling Price - Cost Price) / (Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100.

Marked price = 100 + 10% of 100

⇒ Marked price = 100 + 10

⇒ Marked price = 110

Selling price = Marked price - 5% of Marked price

⇒ Selling price = 110 - 5% of 110

⇒ Selling price = 110 - 5.5

⇒ Selling price = 104.5

Profit Percentage = (Selling Price - Cost Price) / (Cost Price) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (104.5 - 100) / 100 × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 4.5 / 100 × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 4.5%

**The profit percentage is 4.5%, so the correct option is 2.**

questions.question: Rupesh scored 20 percent marks in an exam and failed by 20 marks. If he scores 70 percent marks, then he gets 5 marks more than passing marks. What should be the passing marks for the exam?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 70% − 20% = 50%

Difference in marks = 20 (failed by) + 5 (excess) = 25 marks

∴ 50% of total marks = 25 marks

→ 10% of total marks = 5 marks

Passing marks = (20% of total) + 20 = (2 × 5) + 20 = 30 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1 score = 20% of Total, Deficit from passing = 20 marks

Case 2 score = 70% of Total, Excess over passing = 5 marks

**Formula Used:**

Passing marks = (Score percentage × Total Marks) + Deficit = (Score percentage × Total Marks) − Excess

 
• 20% Marks Fail by 20 Passing Point 70% Marks Extra 5 
 Gap = 50% = 25 Marks 

⇒ Let the total marks be x.

⇒ (20/100) × x + 20 = (70/100) × x − 5

⇒ 0.20x + 20 = 0.70x − 5

⇒ 0.70x − 0.20x = 20 + 5

⇒ 0.50x = 25

⇒ x = 25 ÷ 0.50 = 50

⇒ Passing marks = 20% of 50 + 20

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × 50 + 20

⇒ Passing marks = 10 + 20 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Marks Formula

Total Marks = (Difference in marks obtained ÷ Difference in percentage) × 100.

Passing Percentage

Passing Percentage = (Passing Marks ÷ Total Marks) × 100. It is the minimum percent required to pass the exam.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is used to find growth or reduction in scores.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 36²⁹ is divided by 10?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number = 36²⁹

Divisor = 10

**Formula Used:**

Remainder when a number is divided by 10 is the last digit of the number.

**Calculations:**

The last digit of 36 is 6.

Any power of 6 ends with 6.

Therefore, the last digit of 36²⁹ is 6.

⇒ The remainder when 36²⁹ is divided by 10 is 6.

**Answer:**

The remainder when 36²⁹ is divided by 10 is **6**.

questions.question: The value of a cycle depreciates at the rate of 10% after every year. If at the end of 3 years, its value is Rs. 10,935, then find its purchase price.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The value of the cycle depreciates at the rate of 10% after every year.

At the end of 3 years, its value is Rs. 10,935.

**Formula Used:**

Depreciation formula: Future Value = Present Value × (1 - Depreciation Rate)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Let the purchase price be P.

Future Value = Present Value × (1 - Depreciation Rate)³

10935 = P × (1 - 0.10)³

10935 = P × 0.9³

10935 = P × 0.729

⇒ P = 10935 / 0.729

⇒ P = 15000

**The purchase price of the cycle is Rs. 15,000.**

questions.question: If a mobile is sold at a loss of 25 percent, then what is the respective ratio of cost price and selling price of the mobile?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Loss Percentage = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss Percentage = (Loss / Cost Price) × 100

Selling Price = Cost Price - Loss

Ratio of Cost Price and Selling Price = Cost Price / Selling Price

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100.

Loss = 25% of 100

Loss = (25/100) × 100

Loss = 25

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price - Loss

SP = 100 - 25

SP = 75

Ratio of Cost Price and Selling Price = CP / SP

Ratio = 100 / 75

Ratio = 4 / 3

**The respective ratio of cost price and selling price of the mobile is 4 : 3.**

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 60 km/hr and 95 km/hr. The time taken by faster train to cross a man sitting in the slower train is 36 seconds. What will be the length of the faster train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the slower train = 60 km/hr

Speed of the faster train = 95 km/hr

Time taken by the faster train to cros
s the man in the slower train = 36 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of faster train - Speed of slower train

Length of the faster train = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = 95 km/hr - 60 km/hr

Relative Speed = 35 km/hr

Convert km/hr to m/s:

Relative Speed = 35 × (1000 / 3600) m/s

Relative Speed = 35 × (5 / 18) m/s

Relative Speed = 175 / 18 m/s

Length of the faster train = Relative Speed × Time

Length of the faster train = (175 / 18) × 36

Length of the faster train = 175 × 2

Length of the faster train = 350 meters

**The length of the faster train is 350 meters.**

questions.question: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 3300 is 10 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 2970. What will be the selling price of the article to earn a profit of 30 percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price at profit = Rs. 3300

Selling price at loss = Rs. 2970

Profit = 10 × Loss

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) - Profit

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) + Loss

Required Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit Percentage)

**Calculation:**

Let the loss be L.

Profit = 10L

⇒ 3300 = CP + 10L

⇒ 2970 = CP - L

⇒ 3300 - CP = 10L

⇒ CP - 2970 = L

Adding these equations:

3300 - CP + CP - 2970 = 10L + L

⇒ 3300 - 2970 = 11L

⇒ 330 = 11L

⇒ L = 330 / 11

⇒ L = 30

Now, CP = 2970 + 30

⇒ CP = 3000

To earn a profit of 30%:

Required SP = 3000 × (1 + 30/100)

⇒ Required SP = 3000 × 1.3

⇒ Required SP = 3900

**The selling price of the article to earn a profit of 30 percent is Rs. 3900.**
